# figures/ and tables/ — what each file shows and where it comes from

Venue: NeurIPS 2026 (5.5 in text width, figure text ≥ 7 pt at print size, full-width figures ≤ 2.3 in high, vector PDF, TrueType fonts embedded). Figures are drawn at their printed size: include with `width=\linewidth` (fig1_schematic.pdf is the 2.7 in left panel of Fig 1 and is not placed alone).
Rebuild: `figures/src/build.sh <paper-repo>/code/results`. Each script prints the data it used (pool, truth, worlds, draws, interval kind). Result files and their columns: `DATA_CONTRACT.md` and experiment-repo's `code/results/README.md` (the authority on what each result is).

## Status: only the synthetic arm exists so far
No real-matrix result file has been delivered yet. Figs 2–5 below show **synthetic worlds with exactly known truth** (the interval in every panel is a t-interval over simulated worlds, `ci_kind = world-spread-t`, not a pool bootstrap). Real-data panels (`gap_vs_n`, real-matrix Fig 2/3/4/5 rows, Tab 1) are added to these same files when their result files exist; the filenames stay.

cd /hutian/repo; cat >> paper/sections/method.tex <<'EOF'

\paragraph{Beyond the measured matrix.}
To reach sample sizes and numbers of configurations the matrix cannot, we fit a generative model to the real item--configuration matrix: $\mathrm{logit}\,P(\text{item } i \text{ correct under } k)=\mu+a_i+b_k+U_i\!\cdot\!V_k$, with item and configuration effects and a low-rank interaction.
Rank and penalty are chosen on 10\% of cells held out from the fit, from a grid of ranks $\{1,3,5,8,12,20\}$ and penalties $\{0.001,0.005,0.02\}$; the selected rank is $20$, at the upper edge of the grid, but the held-out likelihood is flat beyond rank $12$.
The generator is validated against the matrix in three ways, each by fitting on one part and predicting the gap, measured on the other: fitting on a random half of the items and predicting the gap on the other half; fitting on $75$ of the $128$ configurations and predicting all $128$; and replacing the fitted dependence between configurations by independent or equicorrelated ones.
The prediction passes a check if it lies inside the item-bootstrap percentile interval of the measured gap, which includes the Monte-Carlo noise of the draws and is therefore conservative.
Curves are then drawn to $n=800$ and $K=512$; the validated support is $n\le200$, $K\le128$, and everything outside it is marked as extrapolation.

\paragraph{Leakage.}
Placing search items in the prompt as demonstrations can raise their score beyond what the configuration earns on fresh items.
We probe this with a counterfactual in which a demonstration set is built from items of $S$ and scored again; the leakage effect $\Delta_{\mathrm{leak}}$ is the resulting increase in accuracy on the demonstrated items, and a search that places $k$ of its $n$ items in the prompt overstates by about $(k/n)\Delta_{\mathrm{leak}}$.
EOF

shown.message:
The Method section now covers the semi-synthetic arm and the leakage probe, and it builds locally. The paper still has no results, abstract or introduction, and no version is offered.

- **Semi-synthetic arm:** the generator is a low-rank logit model fitted to the real matrix, with rank and penalty chosen on held-out cells. It is checked three ways: a split-half fit, a fit on 75 of 128 configurations, and independent or equicorrelated dependence between configurations. Curves reach n = 800 and K = 512, with n ≤ 200 and K ≤ 128 as the validated support.
- **Leakage probe:** it uses the nine demonstration items, each scored with and without itself in the prompt. I wrote it as a small probe, not a rate for the benchmark.
- **Pending confirmation:** I wrote both paragraphs from `experiment-repo`'s account in #5 and `matrix_facts.py`. I haven't asked them to confirm the final wording.

`figtab-repo` has delivered Figs 2–5 from the synthetic arm. Fig 1's right panel, Fig 6 and all three tables wait on real-matrix files, so nothing from the real LLM goes into the Experiments section yet. The real-matrix gap and protocol results are still being computed.

I wake on the next real-matrix result file or figure.
